#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#============================================================================
# run_sim.sh -- compile + run the self-checking testbench for every system-bus
# option, with and without bus back-pressure (Icarus Verilog).
#
#   ./scripts/run_sim.sh                  # all 6 configurations, default seed sweep
#   ./scripts/run_sim.sh AXI4 STALLS      # one configuration, default seed sweep
#   SIM_SEEDS="1 2 3 4" ./scripts/run_sim.sh   # custom seed sweep
#
# Each configuration is compiled once; the constrained-random descriptor-ring
# tier in the TB is then exercised under every seed in $SIM_SEEDS (passed via
# the +SEED plusarg). The stimulus is deterministic per seed, so the sweep is
# reproducible. The script exits non-zero if any (config, seed) fails.
#============================================================================
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p sim/build

# small, fixed seed sweep by default (kept short so CI stays fast)
SEEDS="${SIM_SEEDS:-1 2 3}"

RTL="rtl/pkg/dma_pkg.sv \
     rtl/core/dma_fifo.sv rtl/core/dma_arbiter.sv rtl/core/dma_csr.sv \
     rtl/core/dma_descriptor_fetch.sv rtl/core/dma_data_mover.sv rtl/core/dma_engine_core.sv \
     rtl/core/reset_sync.sv \
     rtl/adapters/gmm_to_avalon.sv rtl/adapters/gmm_to_axi4.sv rtl/adapters/gmm_to_ahb.sv \
     rtl/top/pcie_dma_top.sv \
     sim/models/avalon_mem_model.sv sim/models/axi_mem_model.sv sim/models/ahb_mem_model.sv \
     sim/tb_pcie_dma.sv"

rc=0

run() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  local defs=""
  for d in "$@"; do defs="$defs -D$d"; done
  iverilog -g2012 -Irtl/pkg $defs -s tb_pcie_dma -o sim/build/sim.vvp $RTL 2>sim/build/compile.log
  if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo "$name: COMPILE FAIL"; cat sim/build/compile.log; rc=1; return 1; fi
  local s out
  for s in $SEEDS; do
    out=$(vvp sim/build/sim.vvp +SEED="$s" 2>&1)
    if echo "$out" | grep -q "=== PASS"; then
      echo "$name seed=$s: PASS"
    else
      echo "$name seed=$s: FAIL"; echo "$out" | tail -8; rc=1
    fi
  done
}

if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
  case "$1" in
    AVALON) shift; run "AVALON ${*}" "$@";;
    AXI4)   shift; run "AXI4 ${*}"   USE_AXI "$@";;
    AHB)    shift; run "AHB ${*}"    USE_AHB "$@";;
    *) echo "usage: $0 [AVALON|AXI4|AHB] [STALLS]"; exit 1;;
  esac
else
  run "AVALON        "
  run "AVALON +stalls" STALLS
  run "AXI4          " USE_AXI
  run "AXI4   +stalls" USE_AXI STALLS
  run "AHB           " USE_AHB
  run "AHB    +stalls" USE_AHB STALLS
  # issue #14: exercise the optional 2-FF reset synchronizer (RESET_SYNC=1)
  run "AVALON +rstsyn" RESET_SYNC_EN
fi

exit $rc
#============================================================================
# pcie_dma.sdc -- Timing constraints for the PCIe DMA engine
#
# The whole engine runs on a single clock `clk` (typically the PCIe Hard IP
# application clock coreclkout_hip, 125-250 MHz). Adjust the period to the
# target. Bus ports are constrained relative to clk; tighten with real values
# once integrated.
#============================================================================

# 125 MHz application clock (8 ns). Change to match coreclkout_hip.
create_clock -name clk -period 8.000 [get_ports clk]

derive_clock_uncertainty

# asynchronous, synchronously-deasserted reset.
# This also covers the optional reset_sync (RESET_SYNC=1, see docs IR-1): the
# false path is the asynchronous rst_n input into the first synchronizer flop;
# the synchronized deassertion is then a normal timed path inside the clk domain.
set_false_path -from [get_ports rst_n]

# --- Dual-clock SYS bus (docs/architecture.md IR-2) ----------------------------
# This reference is single-clock: the SYS bus runs on `clk`, so nothing extra is
# needed. If you insert a dual-clock bridge ahead of the gmm_to_* adapter so the
# SYS bus runs on its own clock, define that clock and declare the two groups
# asynchronous so TimeQuest does not time the crossing (constrain the bridge's
# internal CDC per its datasheet). Example (uncomment + adapt once integrated):
#   create_clock -name sys_clk -period <ns> [get_ports sys_clk]
#   set_clock_groups -asynchronous -group {clk} -group {sys_clk}

# Conservative I/O budget: 1 ns for combinational paths to/from pins, applied to
# the data/control ports only (not the clock or reset). These ports are
# internal-facing (virtual pins for standalone fit); when the core is integrated,
# the surrounding fabric provides the real timing.
set_input_delay  -clock clk 1.0 [remove_from_collection [all_inputs] [get_ports {clk rst_n}]]
set_output_delay -clock clk 1.0 [all_outputs]
#============================================================================
# pcie_dma_integration.sdc -- integration timing template for pcie_dma_top
#
# Use this INSTEAD of quartus/pcie_dma.sdc when pcie_dma_top is instantiated as
# a Platform Designer component behind a PCIe Hard IP (the documented primary
# flow), rather than fitted standalone with virtual pins.
#
# Why a separate file:
#   * pcie_dma.sdc creates its own 8 ns `clk` and puts blanket 1 ns I/O delays
#     on the (virtual) bus pins -- correct only for the standalone fit.
#   * When integrated, `clk` is the PCIe Hard IP application clock and the bus
#     ports are internal fabric nets fully timed by Quartus between the
#     connected masters/slaves. No create_clock / I/O delay on those nets.
#
# Edit the marked node paths to match your system, then add this .sdc to the
# project (set_global_assignment -name SDC_FILE pcie_dma_integration.sdc).
#============================================================================

# Always safe: account for PLL/clock-network uncertainty on every clock.
derive_clock_uncertainty

#----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (1) Single-clock deployment  (default; SYS bus on the application clock)
#
# The PCIe Hard IP already constrains its application clock (coreclkout_hip)
# via its own generated .sdc -- do NOT create_clock it again. The whole engine
# runs on that one clock, so no extra clock constraints are needed here.
#
# Reset is active-low and synchronously deasserted, so recovery/removal is a
# false path. Point this at the synchronized reset register feeding the
# component (the Hard IP / reset bridge usually supplies it):
#
#   # set_false_path -from [get_keepers {*reset_sync*}] -to [all_registers]
#----------------------------------------------------------------------------

#----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (2) Separate-SYS-clock deployment  (dual-clock)
#
# Per docs/architecture.md "Clocking / CDC note": when the local system bus
# runs on its own clock through a dual-clock Avalon-MM/AXI clock-crossing
# bridge, the application clock and the SYS clock are asynchronous. Cut the two
# domains so TimeQuest does not try to time cross-domain paths (the bridge
# provides the synchronizers). Set the two clock nodes for your system, then
# uncomment:
#
#   # set app_clk [get_clocks <pcie_inst>|*coreclkout_hip*]
#   # set sys_clk [get_clocks <sys_clk_source>]
#   # set_clock_groups -asynchronous -group $app_clk -group $sys_clk
#----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#============================================================================
# pcie_dma.qsf -- Quartus settings for the PCIe DMA engine
#
# Synthesizes pcie_dma_top as a standalone IP core. The system-bus flavour is
# chosen with the SYS_IF parameter (AVALON | AXI4 | AHB).
#
# This is an IP core meant to be integrated (e.g. as a Platform Designer / Qsys
# component behind the PCIe Hard IP). For a standalone fitter run, the top-level
# bus ports are turned into VIRTUAL_PINs (see virtual_pins.tcl) so the design
# is not constrained by physical pin count.
#
#   quartus_sh --flow compile pcie_dma
#============================================================================

set_global_assignment -name FAMILY "Cyclone V"
set_global_assignment -name DEVICE 5CGXFC9D6F27C7
set_global_assignment -name TOP_LEVEL_ENTITY pcie_dma_top
set_global_assignment -name ORIGINAL_QUARTUS_VERSION 23.1
set_global_assignment -name PROJECT_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY output_files

# language / search
set_global_assignment -name VERILOG_INPUT_VERSION SYSTEMVERILOG_2012
set_global_assignment -name SEARCH_PATH ../rtl/pkg

# package (must be read first)
set_global_assignment -name SYSTEMVERILOG_FILE ../rtl/pkg/dma_pkg.sv

# core
set_global_assignment -name SYSTEMVERILOG_FILE ../rtl/core/dma_fifo.sv
set_global_assignment -name SYSTEMVERILOG_FILE ../rtl/core/dma_arbiter.sv
set_global_assignment -name SYSTEMVERILOG_FILE ../rtl/core/dma_csr.sv
set_global_assignment -name SYSTEMVERILOG_FILE ../rtl/core/dma_descriptor_fetch.sv
set_global_assignment -name SYSTEMVERILOG_FILE ../rtl/core/dma_data_mover.sv
set_global_assignment -name SYSTEMVERILOG_FILE ../rtl/core/dma_engine_core.sv

# adapters

    61 rtl/adapters/gmm_to_avalon.sv
   193 rtl/adapters/gmm_to_axi4.sv
   172 rtl/core/dma_arbiter.sv

# clock uncertainty automatically.)

# normal timed recovery/removal path inside the clk domain.
set_false_path -from [get_ports rst_n]

# the data/control ports only (not the clock or reset), as in the Quartus SDC.
set_input_delay  -clock clk 1.0 [get_ports -filter {DIRECTION == IN && NAME != clk && NAME != rst_n}]
set_output_delay -clock clk 1.0 [all_outputs]

file mkdir $out_dir

CFGBVS-1#1 Warning
Missing CFGBVS and CONFIG_VOLTAGE Design Properties  
Neither the CFGBVS nor CONFIG_VOLTAGE voltage property is set in the current_design.  Configuration bank voltage select (CFGBVS) must be set to VCCO or GND, and CONFIG_VOLTAGE must be set to the correct configuration voltage, in order to determine the I/O voltage support for the pins in bank 0.  It is suggested to specify these either using the 'Edit Device Properties' function in the GUI or directly in the XDC file using the following syntax:

 set_property CFGBVS value1 [current_design]
 #where value1 is either VCCO or GND

 set_property CONFIG_VOLTAGE value2 [current_design]
 #where value2 is the voltage provided to configuration bank 0

Refer to the device configuration user guide for more information.

Neither the CFGBVS nor CONFIG_VOLTAGE voltage property is set in the current_design.  Configuration bank voltage select (CFGBVS) must be set to VCCO or GND, and CONFIG_VOLTAGE must be set to the correct configuration voltage, in order to determine the I/O voltage support for the pins in bank 0.  It is suggested to specify these either using the 'Edit Device Properties' function in the GUI or directly in the XDC file using the following syntax:

 set_property CFGBVS value1 [current_design]
 #where value1 is either VCCO or GND

 set_property CONFIG_VOLTAGE value2 [current_design]

cd "/d/AMD Ross Test/wt/ross-dma/designs/dma" && cat > vivado/README.md <<'EOF'
# Vivado port ΓÇö PCIe scatter-gather DMA engine on Artix-7

Target: `xc7a100tcsg324-1`, top `pcie_dma_top` with `SYS_IF="AXI4"`, `RESET_SYNC=1`,
`clk` = 125 MHz (8.000 ns), out-of-context (no I/O buffers ΓÇö the Vivado
counterpart of the Quartus virtual pins). Tool: Vivado v2025.2 (build 6299465).

**Headline: the design does not meet 125 MHz on this part/speed grade.**
Post-route WNS is **-1.019 ns** (default directives) / **-0.945 ns** (Explore
directives). It closes at a **9.25 ns** period (108.1 MHz). Hold is met, DRC has
no errors, and the xsim regression passes 6/6.

## How to run

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File vivado/run_build.ps1                    # 125 MHz, default directives -> vivado/reports/
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File vivado/run_build.ps1 8.0 explore explore  # 125 MHz, Explore directives -> vivado/reports/explore/
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File vivado/run_build.ps1 9.25 p9_250 default  # other period -> vivado/reports/<tag>/
scripts\run_xsim.bat                                                             # xsim regression (AXI4, AXI4+STALLS; seeds 1 2 3)
```

`run_build.ps1` only launches `vivado -mode batch -source build.tcl [-tclargs <period> <tag> <flow>]`
from `vivado/build/` (git-ignored: checkpoints, scratch) and copies the Vivado
log next to the reports. Override the install location with `VIVADO_BIN`
(build) / `VIVADO_BIN_DIR` (xsim). `SIM_SEEDS="1 2 3 4"` changes the seed sweep.

`build.tcl` steps: `synth_design -lint` ΓåÆ `synth_design -mode out_of_context` ΓåÆ
`opt_design` / `place_design` / `phys_opt_design` / `route_design` ΓåÆ reports
(`utilization`, `utilization_hier`, `timing_summary`, `timing_worst_setup/hold`,
`drc`, `methodology`, `check_timing`, `route_status`, plus post-synth
`utilization_synth` / `timing_summary_synth`).

Committed runs (each directory holds the full report set and `vivado.log`):

| Directory                  | Period   | Directives |
|----------------------------|----------|------------|
| `vivado/reports/`          | 8.000 ns | default    |
| `vivado/reports/explore/`  | 8.000 ns | Explore (`opt` Explore, `place` ExtraTimingOpt, `phys_opt`/`route` AggressiveExplore, post-route `phys_opt`) |
| `vivado/reports/p9_000/`   | 9.000 ns | default    |
| `vivado/reports/p9_250/`   | 9.250 ns | default    |

## Constraints (`pcie_dma.xdc`) vs `quartus/pcie_dma.sdc`

| Quartus SDC | XDC | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `create_clock -period 8.000 clk` | same | |
| `derive_clock_uncertainty` | ΓÇö | Vivado derives it automatically |
| `set_false_path -from rst_n` | same | cuts only the async input of `reset_sync`; the synchronized reset fan-out is timed (recovery/removal, `**async_default**` group) |
| `set_input_delay`/`set_output_delay 1.0` | same value, **`-max` only** | see below |
| virtual pins | `-mode out_of_context` + `HD.CLK_SRC` on `clk` | models clock arrival through a global buffer |
| `altera_attribute` on the synchronizer (RTL) | `ASYNC_REG` on `*u_rst_sync/sync_q_reg*` | set from the XDC, RTL untouched |

**Deviation ΓÇö I/O delays are setup-only.** With min = max = 1.0 ns (the literal
SDC translation) the first run reported WHS = -0.343 ns with 204 failing hold
endpoints, all on input ports: the port-referenced launch edge has no clock
insertion delay while the capture flop sees ~1.8 ns of it. That compares
against a launch flop that does not exist in an OOC run, and it made the
router add hold detours on real nets. Boundary hold therefore is **not checked
here** and must be timed in the integrated design. Consequences visible in the
reports: `check_timing` lists 318 partial input / 580 partial output delays and
`report_methodology` 505 TIMING-18 warnings. (That first run's reports were
overwritten and are not committed; the setup result was the same -1.019 ns.)

## Timing results (post-route)

| Run | Period | WNS | TNS | Failing setup endpoints | WHS | THS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default (`reports/`) | 8.000 ns | **-1.019 ns** | -18.534 ns | 55 / 5248 | 0.034 ns | 0.000 ns |
| Explore (`reports/explore/`) | 8.000 ns | -0.945 ns | -14.309 ns | 40 / 5302 | 0.105 ns | 0.000 ns |
| default (`reports/p9_000/`) | 9.000 ns | -0.334 ns | -2.195 ns | 10 / 5245 | 0.034 ns | 0.000 ns |
| default (`reports/p9_250/`) | 9.250 ns | **+0.047 ns** | 0.000 ns | 0 / 5245 | 0.032 ns | 0.000 ns |

Source: "Design Timing Summary" in each `timing_summary.rpt`. In the 125 MHz
default run the reset recovery/removal group (`**async_default**`) is met
(setup slack 1.275 ns, hold 0.604 ns) and minimum pulse width slack is 2.750 ns.
Post-synthesis estimate at 8 ns was WNS -2.053 ns (`timing_summary_synth.rpt`).

**Achievable Fmax.** Period minus slack at 125 MHz gives 8.000 + 1.019 =
9.019 ns (110.9 MHz) for the default flow and 8.945 ns (111.8 MHz) for Explore,
but that extrapolation was optimistic: an actual run at 9.000 ns still missed
by 0.334 ns. The demonstrated closing point is **9.250 ns = 108.1 MHz**
(WNS +0.047 ns). Nothing between 9.000 and 9.250 ns was run. Results are from
one run per configuration; no placement-seed sweep was done.

**Critical path** (`timing_worst_setup.rpt`): `u_core/u_mover/w_addr_reg[0]` ΓåÆ
`u_core/u_mover/w_burstcount_q_reg[*]/CE` and `w_dcnt_reg[*]/CE`, 8.773 ns data
path, 12 logic levels (5 CARRY4), 46 % logic / 54 % route. This is the write-side
burst sizing in `rtl/core/dma_data_mover.sv`: `beats_to_boundary(w_addr)` (line
106) ΓåÆ `min3(MAX_BURST_BEATS, w_rem, ΓÇª)` (line 140) ΓåÆ comparison against the
FIFO level ΓåÆ write-FSM enable, all in one cycle. All failing endpoints of the
worst paths start at `w_addr`; the same path is the worst one in the Explore
and 9.0 ns runs. Tool directives recovered only 0.074 ns, so closing 125 MHz on
a -1 Artix-7 needs an RTL change (e.g. registering the boundary-limited burst
size when `w_addr` is updated) or a faster speed grade. I did not make that
change: it alters core datapath timing behaviour and would need the full
simulation + formal suite, which is beyond this port.

## Utilization (post-route, 125 MHz default run, `utilization.rpt`)

| Resource | Used | Available | % |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slice LUTs | 1373 | 63400 | 2.17 |
| ΓÇö LUT as logic | 1029 | 63400 | 1.62 |
| ΓÇö LUT as distributed RAM | 344 | 19000 | 1.81 |
| Slice registers (FF) | 825 | 126800 | 0.65 |
| Block RAM tiles | 0 | 135 | 0.00 |
| DSPs | 0 | 240 | 0.00 |

BRAM is 0 because `dma_fifo` reads its memory asynchronously (show-ahead), so
Vivado maps it to LUT RAM ΓÇö the same reason the source notes it maps to MLAB on
Altera. By hierarchy (`utilization_hier.rpt`): `u_mover` 944 LUTs / 244 FFs (of
which `u_fifo` 620 LUTs incl. the 344 LUTRAMs), `u_fetch` 222 / 202, `u_csr`
134 / 169, AXI4 adapter 18 / 50. The Explore run uses 1382 LUTs / 843 FFs.

## DRC / methodology (125 MHz default run)

- `drc.rpt`: 0 errors, 2 warnings ΓÇö CFGBVS-1 (no configuration voltage set;
  irrelevant for an OOC block) and RTSTAT-10 (262 nets with no routable loads:
  the top-level output ports, expected in OOC). `route_status.rpt`: 0 nets with
  routing errors.
- `methodology.rpt`: TIMING-16 ├ù5 (the setup violation above), TIMING-18 ├ù505
  (setup-only I/O delays, see above).

## RTL lint (`synth_design -lint`, `reports/lint.rpt` + lint section of `reports/vivado.log`)

Lint run total: **0 errors, 0 critical warnings, 77 warnings**.

| Source | ID | Count | What | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Linter rule | ASSIGN-10 | 10 | input port bits never read | Not real. 6 are the unselected Avalon/AHB input groups on `pcie_dma_top` (by design for `SYS_IF="AXI4"`); 4 are `axi_bid`/`axi_rid`/`axi_bresp`/`axi_rresp` in `gmm_to_axi4` ΓÇö see note |
| Linter rule | ASSIGN-6 | 2 | `d` and `ctrl_field` bits not read in `dma_descriptor_fetch` | Not real: reserved descriptor bytes / unused control bits (already waived for Verilator in the source) |
| Elaboration | Synth 8-11067 | 52 | `parameter` inside package `dma_pkg` treated as localparam | Not real: correct per the LRM, purely informational |
| Elaboration | Synth 8-7137 | 12 | register "has both Set and reset with same priority" | Real but benign, see note |
| Elaboration | Synth 8-3936 | 1 | `d_reg` trimmed from 256 to 192 bits | Not real: same reserved descriptor bits as ASSIGN-6 |

`lint.rpt` itself contains only the 12 linter-rule violations (all severity
WARNING); the other 65 are elaboration messages emitted during the lint run.

Notes on the two worth reading:

- **Synth 8-7137** (`beats` in `dma_descriptor_fetch.sv:94`, `aw_addr_q` /
  `aw_len_q` in `gmm_to_axi4.sv:117-118`): these registers are assigned inside
  an `always_ff ΓÇª or negedge rst_n` block but are not in its reset branch, so
  the asynchronous reset becomes part of their clock-enable. Behaviour is
  correct (they are always written before being read) and it costs a little
  enable logic; moving them to a separate non-reset `always_ff` would be the
  clean fix. Not changed.
- **`axi_bresp` / `axi_rresp` unread** in `gmm_to_axi4`: I did not trace how the
  adapter's `err` output is derived, so I cannot say whether ignoring the AXI
  response codes is intentional. Flagging it for the design owner rather than
  dismissing it.

## xsim regression (`scripts/run_xsim.bat` ΓåÆ `run_xsim.ps1`)

`xvlog -sv` + `xelab` once per configuration, then `xsim -R` per seed with
`+SEED=<n>`; pass = log contains `=== PASS` (same criterion as `run_sim.sh`).

| Configuration | Defines | seed 1 | seed 2 | seed 3 | Logs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AXI4 | `USE_AXI` | PASS | PASS | PASS | `sim/build/xsim_axi4_seed<n>.log` |
| AXI4 + STALLS | `USE_AXI`, `STALLS` | PASS | PASS | PASS | `sim/build/xsim_axi4_stalls_seed<n>.log` |

Each log ends with `=== PASS : all checks ok ===`. The testbench instantiates
the DUT with its default `RESET_SYNC=0` in these configurations (as in
`run_sim.sh`; `RESET_SYNC=1` is only simulated under `+define+RESET_SYNC_EN`,
which this script does not run), so the synthesized `RESET_SYNC=1` variant is
covered by implementation but not by this regression. xsim's RNG differs from
Icarus, so a given seed produces different (still deterministic) stimulus.

## Source changes

No file under `rtl/` was modified.

One testbench line was changed, `sim/tb_pcie_dma.sv` (seeding):

```
-    void'($urandom(rng_seed));
+    rng_discard = $urandom(rng_seed);      // new: int unsigned rng_discard;
```

xsim rejects the void-cast form at elaboration (`ERROR: [XSIM 43-3122] ΓÇª urandom
system task is not supported`); assigning the result is standard SystemVerilog
and is the same call. **Not re-verified under Icarus:** the only Icarus on this
machine is 11.0, which fails to compile the unmodified `rtl/pkg/dma_pkg.sv`
(`syntax error` at line 27) for every configuration, so `scripts/run_sim.sh`
could not be run here before or after the change.

`.gitignore` gained Vivado/xsim outputs and exceptions so the reports' logs and
`sim/build/xsim_*.log` are tracked.

## Not done

- 125 MHz timing closure (see above).
- Boundary (port) hold analysis; placement-seed sweep; periods between 9.0 and 9.25 ns.
- xsim runs of the AVALON / AHB / `RESET_SYNC_EN` configurations (not requested).
- Icarus re-run after the testbench edit (tool too old locally).
EOF
du -sh vivado/reports sim/build/xsim_*.log | tail -8; cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && git add -A designs/dma && git status --short | head -80

| Quartus SDC | XDC | Note |

| `create_clock -period 8.000 clk` | same | |

updated) or a faster speed grade. I did not make that change: it alters the

no errors, and the xsim regression passes 6/6.

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File vivado/run_build.ps1                      # 125 MHz, default directives -> vivado/reports/
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File vivado/run_build.ps1 8.0 explore explore  # 125 MHz, Explore directives -> vivado/reports/explore/
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File vivado/run_build.ps1 9.25 p9_250 default  # other period -> vivado/reports/<tag>/
scripts\run_xsim.bat                                                               # xsim regression (AXI4, AXI4+STALLS; seeds 1 2 3)

log next to the reports. Override the install location with `VIVADO_BIN`
(build) / `VIVADO_BIN_DIR` (xsim). `SIM_SEEDS="1 2 3 4"` changes the seed sweep.

`opt_design` / `place_design` / `phys_opt_design` / `route_design` ΓåÆ reports
(`utilization`, `utilization_hier`, `timing_summary`, `timing_worst_setup/hold`,
`drc`, `methodology`, `check_timing`, `route_status`, plus post-synth

| Directory                  | Period   | Directives |
|----------------------------|----------|------------|
| `vivado/reports/`          | 8.000 ns | default    |
| `vivado/reports/explore/`  | 8.000 ns | Explore (`opt` Explore, `place` ExtraTimingOpt, `phys_opt`/`route` AggressiveExplore, post-route `phys_opt`) |
| `vivado/reports/p9_000/`   | 9.000 ns | default    |
| `vivado/reports/p9_250/`   | 9.250 ns | default    |

| Quartus SDC | XDC | Note |
|---|---|---|

| `derive_clock_uncertainty` | ΓÇö | Vivado derives it automatically |
| `set_false_path -from rst_n` | same | cuts only the async input of `reset_sync`; the synchronized reset fan-out is timed (recovery/removal, `**async_default**` group) |
| `set_input_delay` / `set_output_delay 1.0` | same value, **`-max` only** | see below |
| virtual pins | `-mode out_of_context` + `HD.CLK_SRC` on `clk` | models clock arrival through a global buffer |
| `altera_attribute` on the synchronizer (RTL) | `ASYNC_REG` on `*u_rst_sync/sync_q_reg*` | set from the XDC, RTL untouched |

endpoints on input ports: the port-referenced launch edge has no clock
insertion delay while the capture flop sees about 1.8 ns of it. That compares
against a launch flop that does not exist in an OOC run. Boundary hold is
therefore **not checked here** and must be timed in the integrated design.

580 partial output delays and `report_methodology` 505 TIMING-18 warnings.

WNS was the same -1.019 ns.)

| Run | Period | WNS | TNS | Failing setup endpoints | WHS | THS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default (`reports/`) | 8.000 ns | **-1.019 ns** | -18.534 ns | 55 / 5248 | 0.034 ns | 0.000 ns |

dma: add Vivado OOC flow for Artix-7 (xc7a100tcsg324-1)

Non-project build.tcl (lint, synth, opt/place/phys_opt/route, reports) for
pcie_dma_top with SYS_IF="AXI4", RESET_SYNC=1, plus pcie_dma.xdc ported from
quartus/pcie_dma.sdc (125 MHz clk, rst_n false path, 1 ns setup-only I/O
budget, ASYNC_REG on the reset synchronizer). Optional tclargs select another
clock period and the Explore directive set.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git add scripts/run_xsim.bat scripts/run_xsim.ps1 sim/tb_pcie_dma.sv && git add -f sim/build/xsim_axi4_seed*.log sim/build/xsim_axi4_stalls_seed*.log && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
dma: add xsim regression for AXI4 and AXI4+STALLS

scripts/run_xsim.{bat,ps1} compile tb_pcie_dma once per configuration and run
seeds 1 2 3 with the run_sim.sh pass criterion; logs for the 6 passing runs
are in sim/build/.

Testbench: assign the result of the seeding $urandom(seed) call instead of
void-casting it, which xsim rejects (XSIM 43-3122). Not re-run under Icarus
(local Icarus 11.0 cannot compile the unmodified dma_pkg.sv).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git add vivado/README.md vivado/reports && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
dma: Vivado results and README

Reports and logs for the 125 MHz runs (default and Explore directives) and
the 9.0 / 9.25 ns period probes. 125 MHz is not met (WNS -1.019 ns default,
-0.945 ns Explore); timing closes at 9.25 ns. No RTL changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git status --short; git log --oneline | head -4

The port is committed on `ross/dma` (3 commits, not pushed), but the design does **not** meet 125 MHz on `xc7a100tcsg324-1`: post-route WNS is ΓêÆ1.019 ns.

| Deliverable | Status |
|---|---|
| 1. Vivado flow (`vivado/build.tcl`, `vivado/pcie_dma.xdc`) | Runs end to end (lint, synth, opt/place/route, reports); **timing at 125 MHz fails** |
| 2. xsim regression (`scripts/run_xsim.bat` / `.ps1`) | **6/6 PASS** (AXI4 and AXI4+STALLS, seeds 1 2 3), logs in `sim/build/` |
| 3. `vivado/README.md` | Written; numbers come from the committed reports and logs, except two figures quoted from an earlier constraints run whose reports were overwritten (README says so) |

## Timing (post-route)

| Run | Period | WNS | TNS | WHS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default directives | 8.000 ns | **ΓêÆ1.019 ns** | ΓêÆ18.534 ns | +0.034 ns |
| Explore directives | 8.000 ns | ΓêÆ0.945 ns | ΓêÆ14.309 ns | +0.105 ns |
| default | 9.000 ns | ΓêÆ0.334 ns | ΓêÆ2.195 ns | +0.034 ns |
| default | 9.250 ns | **+0.047 ns** | 0 | +0.032 ns |

- **Fmax:** the demonstrated closing period is 9.25 ns (108.1 MHz). Period minus slack suggests about 9.02 ns, but the actual 9.0 ns run still missed, so I would not rely on that extrapolation.
- **Critical path:** write-side burst sizing in `rtl/core/dma_data_mover.sv`, from `w_addr` through `beats_to_boundary` and `min3` to the write-FSM enables, 12 logic levels in one cycle. Closing 125 MHz needs an RTL pipeline stage there or a faster speed grade; I did not make that change.

## Utilization (125 MHz default run)

- **LUTs:** 1373 (1029 logic + 344 distributed RAM)
- **FFs:** 825
- **BRAM:** 0 ΓÇö the FIFO reads asynchronously, so it maps to LUT RAM
- **DSP:** 0

## Lint

The lint run gave 0 errors, 0 critical warnings and 77 warnings; none is a functional bug.

- **Linter rules (12):** 10 ASSIGN-10 and 2 ASSIGN-6, all unread bits that are intentional (unselected bus inputs, reserved descriptor bits, unused AXI ID and response bit 0).
- **Elaboration messages (65):** 52 package-parameter notices, 1 register trim, and 12 Synth 8-7137. The last is real but benign: `beats`, `aw_addr_q` and `aw_len_q` sit in async-reset blocks without a reset branch, so the reset ends up in their clock enable.

DRC has 0 errors and 2 warnings, both expected for an out-of-context block.

## Changes and deviations

- **RTL:** nothing under `rtl/` was modified.
- **Testbench:** one line in `sim/tb_pcie_dma.sv` changed, because xsim rejects `void'($urandom(seed))`; the result is now assigned to a dummy variable. I could not re-run the Icarus regression to confirm it is unaffected: the local Icarus 11.0 fails on the untouched `dma_pkg.sv`.
- **I/O delays are setup-only (`-max`):** the literal min = max = 1 ns translation produced 204 spurious hold failures on input ports, so hold at the module boundary is not checked here.
- **Sim logs:** the six xsim logs are committed with `git add -f`, since a repo-root rule ignores every `build/` directory.

## Not done

- 125 MHz timing closure.
- No placement-seed sweep, and no period between 9.0 and 9.25 ns was tried.
- The xsim runs use the testbench default `RESET_SYNC=0`, so the synthesized `RESET_SYNC=1` variant is implemented but not simulated.
